question: What the arrow drawn along a selected unit's way is made of.

structs.name: CUnitArrow
structs.comment: The arrow drawn on the map along the way a selected unit is going: a band along a Catmull-Rom curve through the provinces of its path, hollow ahead of the unit and filled behind it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
structs.evidence: `operator_new(0x160)` in CUnit::MakeArrow (rva 0x1CC230) before the constructor at rva 0x47F250, which calls the C3dVisibleObject constructor first and writes the table at VA 0x15E3C14; the RTTI export names that table CUnitArrow with C3dVisibleObject as its base.

addresses.name: CUnit::MakeArrow
addresses.comment: **Makes the arrow drawn along a selected unit's way.** Null for a unit with no graphics owner or no path. Its points are the unit's own place - its stack's point plus the province's label point - and the unit point of every province of the path, x moved by the map's width where that is the short way round, each with a height of 0.02 over land and 0 over sea; a fleet starts and ends at a naval base position where it is in a land province, a wing at an air base. A point is added 5 beyond each end in line with the end's leg. The type is looked up by name: `unitInvasionArrow`, `retreatArrow`, `attackArrow`, `stratArrow` under order type 0x5A4, else `moveArrow`. Then `new 0x160` and the CUnitArrow constructor, and the arrow's +0x15C is set to movement_progress over CUnit::PathDistance. Callers: CUnit::ShowMoving and CUnit::EnterProvince, both only for a selected unit, and CUnit::RemakeArrow. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: The five literals; `operator_new(0x160)` before the call of 0x87F250; the walk of [unit+0x138] reading each province's template +0x64/+0x68; the two blocks subtracting `normalised difference * [0x160A508]` (5.0) from the first and the last point; the store at `[arrow+0x15c]`. Bare `ret`, the unit in ECX.

addresses.name: CUnit::RemakeArrow
addresses.comment: Frees the unit's arrow (+0x188) where it has one, through CUnit::FreeArrow, and stores a new one from CUnit::MakeArrow. CUnit::AdvanceMovement calls it on an arrival. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: `cmp [edi+0x188],0`, the call of 0x5CB920 with the field's address, the call of 0x5CC230 and the store. Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CUnit::FreeArrow
addresses.comment: Hides an arrow, takes it out of the scene of the unit's graphics owner (+0x160) and destroys it through CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject, then stores null where it was held. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: the arrow's slot 14 (+0x38), the owner's slot 15, the call of CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject and `mov dword ptr [param],0`. `ret 4`, the unit in EAX.

addresses.name: CUnitArrow::CUnitArrow
addresses.no_signature: the type in ECX and the object first of six stack arguments
addresses.comment: The arrow's constructor: the C3dVisibleObject constructor, the table at VA 0x15E3C14, the type at +0x138, and a copy of the list of points it is given into the vector at +0x14C - a point within 0.1 of the next is dropped. Ends by calling CUnitArrow::BuildMesh. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: `mov dword ptr [esi],0x15e3c14`; the walk of the list with the three compares against the double at 0x160A3C0 (0.1) and the push_back 0x84D3A0 on +0x14C; the call of 0x87FA30. `ret 0x18`.

addresses.name: CUnitArrow::BuildMesh
addresses.comment: **Makes the band of an arrow out of its points.** For each leg between two real points, twenty times: a point of `D3DXVec3CatmullRom` through the four points round the leg at `t = k / 20`, a second at `t + 0.05` for the direction, the direction turned a quarter in the ground plane and - from the second leg on - averaged with the cut before's; two vertices 2.0 either side. The texture's column is 0.5 for the shaft and, within 4.0 of the end, `0.5 + 0.5 * clamp(1 - distance * 0.25, 0, 1)`: the head is the right half of the picture over the last four units. Each vertex carries its cut's number over the number of cuts, which gfx/FX/arrow.fx compares with CurrentProgress to choose the filled half of the texture or the outlined one. So the band is 4 map units wide whatever the arrowType's `size` says. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: The two calls of D3DXVec3CatmullRom with `(double)k / [0x160A318]` (20.0) and that plus [0x160A850] (0.05); the multiplications by [0x160A360] (2.0) either side; the default [0x15AB304] (0.5) and the branch on [0x171DF34] (4.0) with [0x160A258] (0.25); the loop bound `< 0x14`; the store of `(index >> 1) / (count * 0.5)` at vertex +0xC. `ret 8`. And a screenshot of the running game: shaft lines 1 map unit apart and a head 3.3 wide, which are the texture's 18 and 52 rows of 64 on a band 4 wide.

struct_fields.name: type
struct_fields.comment: The `arrowType` the arrow was made from, by name out of the object-type registry. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: `param_1[0x4e] = this` in the constructor, the type arriving in ECX.

struct_fields.name: mesh
struct_fields.comment: The vertex and index buffers CUnitArrow::BuildMesh makes, a 0x24-byte holder; freed and made again on each call. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: `operator_new(0x24)` stored at [arrow+0x148] at the head of 0x87FA30.

struct_fields.name: points_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of the arrow's control points, 12 bytes each - x, height, y - ending at +0x150: the point added before the start, the unit's place, the unit point of each province of the path, and the point added beyond the end. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: The push_back in the constructor; `(end - begin) / 0xc - 2` as the leg count in 0x87FA30.

struct_fields.name: points_end
struct_fields.comment: One past the last control point (see +0x14C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.

struct_fields.name: progress
struct_fields.comment: How much of the arrow is drawn filled, 0 to 1: the unit's movement_progress over CUnit::PathDistance. Written by CUnit::MakeArrow and each hour by CUnit::AdvanceMovement; the shader's CurrentProgress. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.

struct_fields.name: arrow
struct_fields.comment: The selected unit's movement arrow, made by CUnit::MakeArrow and freed by CUnit::FreeArrow. CUnit::AdvanceMovement writes the share of the path walked into its +0x15C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: The store of 0x5CC230's result in CUnit::ShowMoving, CUnit::EnterProvince and CUnit::RemakeArrow.
struct_fields.revises: typed, now that the class it points to is declared

struct_fields.name: stack_points
struct_fields.comment: five points of three floats, one per stack: where each of the province's stacks stands, **as an offset from the province's label point** (+0x5C/+0x60) - CUnit::MakeArrow adds the label point to one to start its arrow there. **Point 0 (+0xCC) is for a land or sea unit with no path, point 1 (+0xD8) for one with a path, point 4 (+0xFC) for an air unit**; 2 and 3 are the two sides of a battle. CUnit::EnterProvince, CUnit::ShowMoving, CUnit::AdvanceMovement and CUnit::CancelMovement all pick that way. No writer was found. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: The 12-byte reads at +0xCC, +0xD8 and +0xFC in 0x5BEFD0 and 0x5C9E10; in 0x5CC230 the arithmetic `stack - (unit point - label) + unit point` for the arrow's first point.
struct_fields.revises: adds that the points are offsets from the label point

slots_noted: none of these is a virtual
